title: The Unknown by David Cale at Studio Seaview #theunknownplay #seanhaye...
transcript: In another home run from Sean Hayes, David Cale, and Leigh Silverman, The Unknown is a new solo thriller with a meta dimension that ripens like a fine wine. Elliott is a writer who initially finds himself in a confusing and unnerving situation with someone who seems to be stalking him. Over time, it becomes debatable whether he's more the subject of an obsession or the obsessive one. It's a twisty and riveting mind bender brought to life by Sean Hayes who continues to impress me with his range and consistently captivating presence. The play is also just good, unfolding in a cleverly satisfying way. While there are aspects of it that feel slightly predictable in retrospect, you can't deny its skillful construction, one that keeps you undeniably hooked throughout the viewing. There's a nice balance between this production's simple and gestural staging with the precision in David Cale’s writing that allows you to visualise the story like you would with an audiobook, while still appreciating the immediacy of Sean Hayes delivering it on stage. Ultimately, my highest praise for this piece is that it provides a specifically gripping experience that I think few solo pieces can achieve. With that, another program for my collection.
